post_message: Switching from one vaccine to another is just a matter of out with the old, in with the new, right? Not exactly.   As more than 30 co-authors, including Sabin's Kate Hopkins, PhD, MPH, report in "Accelerating Evidence-Informed Vaccine Introductions: Lessons from the Hexavalent Early Adopters Workshop" in the new issue of the journal Vaccines, there are multiple considerations when bringing a new immunization into a country's immunization schedule, including complex system changes requiring coordinated governance, reliable data systems, domestic financing, and multisectoral collaboration.  The paper presents evidence-based insights on making a successful switch from National Immunization Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs) and Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) programs of 10 African countries, as well as World Health Organization African Region, Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and consortium partners, who gathered in Senegal last November. It shows the power of Sabin's Regional Peer Learning model/capabilities and helps strengthen policy and operational readiness for countries at different stages of decision-making, planning, and implementation. post_message: Seeing headlines about the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak? Kelly Warfield, Sabin’s President of Research & Development and an expert on this kind of virus, explains why not all Ebola vaccines are the same, and why more research in this area is so needed. ⤵️  “Vaccines developed against Ebola Zaire (EBOV) or Ebola Sudan (SUDV) may not be effective against disease caused by Ebola Bundibugyo (BDBV), such as the ongoing outbreak in DRC and Uganda, because these viruses are genetically and antigenically distinct species within the Ebolavirus genus.    Most Ebola vaccines induce targeted immune responses — particularly antibodies and T cell responses — against the viral glycoprotein (GP) of a specific species. Because the GP sequence and antigenic structure differ between Zaire, Sudan, and Bundibugyo viruses, immune responses elicited by a vaccine targeting one species may not adequately recognize or neutralize another.   While there is some early data indicating ways we might achieve protection against BDBV with existing EBOV and SUDV vaccines, further research is needed to determine whether any licensed Ebola Zaire and/or investigational Sudan vaccines can provide meaningful protection against the distinct Bundibugyo virus. Additionally, new vaccine candidates specifically targeting BDBV should be generated and tested to help address the growing threat of the virus.”  More on the Bundibugyo outbreak from the New York Times:  https://ow.ly/t1UO50Z1H39

post_message: Stop TB Partnership and Sabin Vaccine Institute have entered into a groundbreaking new partnership bringing together TB and Essential Programme on Immunization (EPI) communities within countries to support readiness when the new tuberculosis (#TB) vaccines are introduced.  #Tuberculosis remains the world’s deadliest infectious disease, causing an estimated 1.25 to 1.5 million deaths each year. Stop TB Partnership and Sabin's Boost Community are uniquely primed to connect the immunization and TB communities, to facilitate the generation of actionable evidence, and to build the relationships and shared knowledge needed for an effective preparation and roll-out by countries. post_message: Stop TB Partnership and Sabin Vaccine Institute have entered into a groundbreaking new partnership bringing together TB and Essential Programme on Immunization (EPI) communities within countries to support readiness when the new tuberculosis (#TB) vaccines are introduced.  #Tuberculosis remains the world’s deadliest infectious disease, causing an estimated 1.25 to 1.5 million deaths each year. Infants and children are at particularly high risk, as are people with weakened immune systems. The partnership comes at a crucial time, as countries look ahead to new vaccine candidates that could better protect adolescents and adults, who account for the majority of TB transmission, and offer stronger protection against drug-resistant TB.   Stop TB Partnership and Sabin's Boost Community are uniquely primed to connect the immunization and TB communities, to facilitate the generation of actionable evidence, and to build the relationships and shared knowledge needed for an effective preparation and roll-out by countries. post_message: Switching from one vaccine to another is just a matter of out with the old, in with the new, right? Not exactly.   As more than 30 co-authors, including Sabin's Kate Hopkins, PhD, MPH, report in "Accelerating Evidence-Informed Vaccine Introductions: Lessons from the Hexavalent Early Adopters Workshop" in the new issue of the journal Vaccines, there are multiple considerations when bringing a new immunization into a country's immunization schedule, including complex system changes requiring coordinated governance, reliable data systems, domestic financing, and multisectoral collaboration.  The paper presents evidence-based insights on making a successful switch from National Immunization Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs) and Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) programs of 10 African countries, as well as World Health Organization African Region, Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and consortium partners, who gathered in Senegal last November. It shows the power of Sabin's Regional Peer Learning model/capabilities and helps strengthen policy and operational readiness for countries at different stages of decision-making, planning, and implementation.  See the new article: https://ow.ly/ShmS50Z2nva
